changes.after: Rust can let you change a value once its shared borrow is no longer needed.

before: The compiler can determine that a shared borrow is no longer used after its final access. Its effective restriction need not last to the closing brace.
Here view is printed before text.push, so the shared borrow is no longer needed when mutation begins.
If text.push occurs before a later print of view, the mutable access overlaps a still-needed shared borrow and is rejected.
No runtime borrow counter is used for these ordinary references. Later RefCell has a different runtime-checked mechanism.
Expected output or behavior: moon. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

before.question: Move text.push before the print of view. What happens?
choices: Compilation fails because mutation overlaps a shared borrow that is still used later.
It always compiles because the variables have different names.
The print silently switches to an empty String.
before.explanation: The later read keeps the shared borrow needed across the attempted mutation.

after.question: Can the program add the mark before it prints `view`?
choices: No. The view still needs the borrowed text.
Yes. The view owns a separate copy.
Yes. Rust moves the print automatically.
after.explanation: The later print still needs the shared view. Rust refuses the earlier change.
